facts.statement: Pinpanetta fossils date to the Late Oligocene.
The genus Pinpanetta was described by Worthy in 2009.
Pinpanetta is an extinct genus of birds belonging to the duck family.
facts.quote: Pinpanetta is an extinct genus of birds, in the duck family

facts.statement: Pinpanetta lived in central Australia during the Late Oligocene.
facts.quote: from the Late Oligocene of central Australia

facts.statement: The genus name Pinpanetta is derived from Lake Pinpa in the Lake Eyre Basin of north-eastern South Australia.
facts.quote: The genus name comes from Lake Pinpa, in the Lake Eyre Basin of north-eastern South Australia

facts.statement: Much of the descriptive fossil material for Pinpanetta comes from the Pinpa Local Fauna.
facts.quote: with reference to the Pinpa Local Fauna from which much of the descriptive fossil material derives

facts.statement: The genus Pinpanetta includes three species: P. tedfordi, P. vickersrichae, and P. fromensis.
facts.quote: It comprises three species: P. tedfordi Worthy, 2009 (type species) P. vickersrichae Worthy, 2009 P. fromensis Worthy, 2009

facts.statement: Pinpanetta belongs to the subfamily Erismaturinae.
Pinpanetta is classified within the family Anatidae.
Pinpanetta lived between 27.3 and 23.04 million years ago during the Chattian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Chattian (27.3 to 23.04 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The specific part of the genus name refers to the Greek word netta, meaning duck.

rejected.statement: Pinpanetta is a member of the class Aves.
